overview: White answers the mirrored 1...h5 with 2.g4, striking at the h5 pawn and opening the h-file. The usual reply 2...hxg4 3.hxg4 Rxh1 4.Bxh1 trades rooks and leaves White with a loose g4 pawn and a bishop on h1, so the material is level but White's kingside is wrecked. Black can instead ignore the pawn and play ...e5 and ...Nf6 with a healthy centre. It is a joke-grade line seen almost only in blitz.

white_ideas.idea: Trade on g4 and h1, then use the bishop on h1 down the long diagonal
Hit the g4 pawn with Black's own advance g5-based tricks is not available, so build with d4, Nc3 and Nf3

black_ideas.idea: Take on g4, trade rooks, then target the weak g4 pawn with ...Nf6 and ...Bg4
Decline with ...e5 and develop normally against a weakened kingside

typical_structures.structure: White with an isolated g4 pawn and no h-pawn, king uncomfortable on either wing

character.notes: Kingside pawns are advanced on both flanks and the h-file opens at once, so the king safety of both sides is in question early.

gambit.notes: 2...hxg4 3.hxg4 returns the pawn immediately and Rxh1 Bxh1 is an even rook trade, so no material is lost on the main line despite the name.

soundness.notes: 2.g4 weakens White's own king for no gain; Black simply develops and has the easier game.

structure.notes: Flank pawns move first and the centre is untouched, so it stays undecided.

approach.notes: Strong players essentially never choose it; it is a blitz curiosity.

level.notes: No theory, but White is the side studying it and it is not a good repertoire choice.

sublines_that_differ.name: Decline
sublines_that_differ.how: Black develops and leaves White to deal with the loosened pawns.

character.reason: Both kingsides are loosened and the h-file opens immediately, so errors are punished fast.

gambit.reason: The pawn on g4 comes straight back after 2...hxg4 3.hxg4, so no material is truly given despite the name.

soundness.reason: White weakens their own king with 2.g4 and gains nothing concrete for it.

structure.reason: Only flank pawns have moved and the centre stays undecided.

approach.reason: Strong players essentially never play 1.h3 h5 2.g4.

level.reason: A dubious line is never Beginner and there is no theory to demand Advanced.

plans.reason: No recognisable plan from the table is characteristic of this line.
